subject: dsa
title: Distinct Subsequences
summary: dp[i][j] is the number of distinct ways to form t's first j chars as a subsequence of s's first i chars. Always carry dp[i-1][j], and when the current chars match also add dp[i-1][j-1].
problem: Count the distinct subsequences of s = "bbb" that equal t = "bb". Rows are prefixes of s ("", b, bb, bbb); columns are prefixes of t ("", b, bb). dp[i][j] is the number of ways to form t's first j chars from s's first i chars.

steps.caption: Rows are s "bbb", columns are t "bb". An empty t has exactly 1 way to form: take nothing from s.
Column 0 is all 1: any prefix of s forms the empty t one way. The empty s forms a nonempty t in 0 ways.
Row b: dp[1][1] = dp[0][1] + dp[0][0] = 0 + 1 = 1 since b equals b. So row b is [1,1,0].
Row bb gives [1,2,1] and row bbb gives [1,3,3]; each matching cell adds the value above and the value above-left.
The bottom-right cell is dp[3][2] = 3, so "bbb" has 3 distinct subsequences equal to "bb".
